records.relationship: Supports (integral to) PR.IR-01: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage
records.relationship_explanation:
The PEP can prevent unauthorized access to the portions of the enterprise that it guards. It can be deployed to protect and segregate discrete network segments. Network segmentation may also be provided by other mechanisms besides a PEP.

In addition, to support ZTA, the data plane and control plane (networks) must be logically separate. The PEP is the only component that can send and receive messages from both planes. It protects the planes from each other and ensures that the control plane is not directly accessible by enterprise assets and resources.

Manages and secures enterprise desktop computers, laptops, and/or mobile devices in accordance with enterprise policy to protect applications and data; ensure device compliance; mitigate and remediate vulnerabilities and threats; monitor for suspicious activity to prevent and detect intrusions; prevent, detect, and disable malware, viruses, and other malicious or unauthorized traffic; repair infected files when possible; provide alerts and recommend remediation actions; and encrypt data.
Pushes enterprise applications and updates to devices, enables users to download enterprise applications that they are authorized to access, remotely deletes all applications and data from devices if needed, tracks user activity on devices, and detects and addresses security issues on the device.
records.relationship: Supports (example of) DE.CM-03: Personnel activity and technology usage are monitored to find potentially adverse events
records.relationship_explanation: The UEM/MDM can monitor user activity for suspicious behavior.

records.architecture_component: Endpoint Security - Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR)/ Endpoint Protection Platform (EPP)
records.component_function: Detects and stops threats to endpoints through an integrated suite of endpoint protection technologies including antivirus, data encryption, intrusion prevention, EDR, and data loss prevention (DLP). May include mechanisms that are designed to protect applications and data; ensure device compliance with policies regarding hardware, firmware, software, and configuration; monitor endpoints for vulnerabilities, suspicious activity, intrusion, infection, and malware; block unauthorized traffic; disable malware and repair infections; manage and administer software and updates; monitor behavior and critical data; and enable endpoints to be tracked, troubleshooted, and wiped, if necessary.
records.relationship: Is supported by (precedes) ID.AM-01: Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained
records.relationship_explanation: For a device to have EDR/EPP software installed on it, the device must be known to be part of the organization’s inventory.

records.relationship: Supports (example of) PR.IR-01: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage
records.relationship_explanation: The PEP can prevent unauthorized access to the portions of the enterprise that it guards. If it is used to protect a single resource, it does not necessarily provide network segregation or network segmentation. However, it can be deployed to protect and segregate discrete network segments. Network segmentation may also be provided by other mechanisms besides a PEP. To support ZTA, the data plane and control plane (networks) must be logically separate. The PEP is the only component that can send and receive messages from both planes. It protects the planes from each other and ensures that the control plane is not directly accessible by enterprise assets and resources.

records.architecture_component: Endpoint Security - Unified Endpoint Management (UEM)/Mobile Device Management (MDM)
records.component_function:
Manages and secures enterprise desktop computers, laptops, and/or mobile devices in accordance with enterprise policy to protect applications and data; ensure device compliance; mitigate and remediate vulnerabilities and threats; monitor for suspicious activity to prevent and detect intrusions; prevent, detect, and disable malware, viruses, and other malicious or unauthorized traffic; repair infected files when possible; provide alerts and recommend remediation actions; and encrypt data.

Pushes enterprise applications and updates to devices, enables users to download enterprise applications that they are authorized to access, remotely deletes all applications and data from devices if needed, tracks user activity on devices, and detects and addresses security issues on the device.
records.relationship: Is supported by (precedes) ID.AM-01: Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained
records.relationship_explanation: IBM Security MaaS360 involves device enrollment into a UEM/MDM system. The device must be known to be part of the organization’s inventory before it can be enrolled.

records.relationship_explanation: Ivanti Sentry segregates a resource/application from the rest of the network, thereby helping to protect the resource/application from unauthorized access by entities located on the rest of the network. A key component of the Ivanti UEM platform is Ivanti Sentry, an inline gateway that manages, encrypts, and secures traffic between mobile devices and back-end enterprise systems. Sentry addresses three fundamental needs: mobile security, scalability, and user experience. Sentry prevents unauthorized interception and malicious manipulation of data through its support for certificate-based authentication. Sentry can encrypt email attachments to protect them from unauthorized apps or cloud services. Sentry ensures the integrity of mobile app traffic by restricting access to the correct corporate destinations and applications. Sentry supports certificate-based SSO authentication, which can eliminate the need for users to enter their username and password when accessing email, intranet sites, and corporate data behind the firewall. Sentry provides on-demand, app-specific VPNs, greatly improving user experience by eliminating the need for manually enabling device-wide VPNs.

records.relationship: Supports (example of) PR.IR-01: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage
records.relationship_explanation: Ivanti Tunnel enables remote users' access to the enterprise via a mobile-first per-app tunnel that helps protect the enterprise network and its resources from unauthorized remote access. Ivanti Tunnel allows organizations to authorize any enterprise-managed app, including in-house and third-party apps, to access resources on the enterprise network using a secure connection. Full Device or Per-App VPNs can be established over any network, including public Wi-Fi networks and cellular networks to ensure business data is always secure. Ivanti Tunnel also leverages Ivanti UEM's advanced closed-loop compliance engine to ensure that jailbroken and otherwise noncompliant devices are not allowed to access sensitive enterprise data. Sentry enables secure data in transit by encrypting communications from modern mobile devices to the enterprise network using strong TLS. PKI-based authentication to Tunnel allows end users to seamlessly authenticate to the back-end resources behind Ivanti Tunnel.

Detects and stops threats to endpoints through an integrated suite of endpoint protection technologies including antivirus, data encryption, intrusion prevention, EDR, and data loss prevention (DLP). May include mechanisms that are designed to protect applications and data; ensure device compliance with policies regarding hardware, firmware, software, and configuration; monitor endpoints for vulnerabilities, suspicious activity, intrusion, infection, and malware; block unauthorized traffic; disable malware and repair infections; manage and administer software and updates; monitor behavior and critical data; and enable endpoints to be tracked, troubleshooted, and wiped, if necessary.
Is supported by (precedes) PR.PS-01: Configuration management practices are established and applied

Configuration management is supported through policies defined in the management console. Logging of all admin actions is available from the Audit tab of the console and optionally shared to an external log server such as a SIEM.

Guards the trust zone that hosts an enterprise resource; enables, monitors, and terminates the connection between subject and resource; forwards requests to and receives commands from the PA
Supports (example of) PR.IR-01: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage

Microsoft Entra Application Proxy is the Policy Enforcement Point for access to on-premises applications for those who own Microsoft Entra ID without Microsoft SSE.
Microsoft Entra Application Proxy provides internet-facing connectivity to on-premises web-based resources without building a DMZ by relying on an outbound HTTPS connection to tunnel the traffic to the resources and back. It provides access to resources in the cloud and on-premises networks for users who are authorized.

records.component_function: Manages access to resources by performing user and device authentication (e.g., SSO and MFA) and using identity, role, and access attributes to determine which access requests are authorized.
records.relationship: Is supported by (precedes) PR.AA-02: Identities are proofed and bound to credentials based on the context of interactions
records.relationship_explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Entra Verified ID support tying higher identity assurance to credential issuance. 
Microsoft Entra ID represents users, services, and devices as the organization directory and authenticates them in a variety of protocols.
Microsoft Entra ID's tokens are signed (verified), encrypted in transit, and can be configured to be encrypted per relying party. User authentications to Entra ID can be configured to require higher assurance methods such as MFA and phishing resistance.
Microsoft Entra Conditional Access which is part of Entra ID along with Microsoft SSE can be used to enforce networking segments, target different types of resources with different policies, and set a higher bar for credentials for different types of access. Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Manager is part of Entra ID, which can be used to configure just-in-time access and set up least privilege.

Microsoft Entra ID
Manages access to resources by performing user and device authentication (e.g., SSO and MFA) and using identity, role, and access attributes to determine which access requests are authorized.
Supports (integral to) PR.AA-03: Users, services, and hardware are authenticated

Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Entra Verified ID support tying higher identity assurance to credential issuance. 
Microsoft Entra ID represents users, services, and devices as the organization directory and authenticates them in a variety of protocols.
Microsoft Entra ID's tokens are signed (verified), encrypted in transit, and can be configured to be encrypted per relying party. User authentications to Entra ID can be configured to require higher assurance methods such as MFA and phishing resistance.
Devices are authenticated via Microsoft Intune, which integrates with Entra Conditional Access, as part of Entra ID to ensure that only onboarded, compliant, and authenticated devices have access to resources.

records.architecture_component: Endpoint Security - Unified Endpoint Management (UEM)/Mobile Device Management (MDM)
records.component_function:
Manages and secures enterprise desktop computers, laptops, and/or mobile devices in accordance with enterprise policy to protect applications and data; ensure device compliance; mitigate and remediate vulnerabilities and threats; prevent, detect, and disable malware, viruses, and other malicious or unauthorized traffic; repair infected files when possible; provide alerts and recommend remediation actions; and encrypt data.

Pushes enterprise applications and updates to devices, enables users to download enterprise applications that they are authorized to access, remotely deletes all applications and data from devices if needed, tracks user activity on devices, and detects and addresses security issues on the device.

records.relationship: Supports (integral to) ID.RA-01: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded
records.relationship_explanation:
Microsoft Intune can detect vulnerabilities such as unpatched devices or unacceptable OS versions. Microsoft Defender for Endpoint is able to monitor for active vulnerabilities such as malware launches or malicious link invocations.
Microsoft Intune supports controls to wipe data and remove applications from devices. 
Microsoft Intune supports defining acceptable device compliance posture and enforcing end user action to meet vulnerability management policy.
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint is able to monitor suspicious activity on the device and report this to Microsoft Intune to mark the device as non-compliant or to Microsoft Entra to block user access.
Microsoft Intune and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint together provide the full spectrum of containment controls (remove unknown apps or malware, block disreputable apps, monitor links and processes launched on the endpoint).
Microsoft Intune and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint together provide the full spectrum of monitoring capabilities (device and OS patch level, settings, and application configuration as well as user activity and links/processes launched on the endpoint). 
Microsoft Intune supports replacing software, updating it, and forcing the device user to remediate vulnerabilities.

records.product: Radiant Logic RadiantOne Intelligent Identity Data Platform
records.component_function: Aggregates and correlates all attributes relating to an identity or object that is being authorized by a ZTA. It enables users of one domain to securely access data or systems of another domain seamlessly, and without the need for completely redundant user administration. Federated identity encompasses the traditional ICAM data, supports identities that may be part of a larger federated ICAM community, and may include non-enterprise employees.
records.relationship: Is supported by (precedes) GV.RR-02: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, understood, and enforced
records.relationship_explanation: The core function of the RadiantOne Identity Data Manager (IDDM) is to abstract identity and credential data from multiple disparate sources of truth and build an aggregated 360-degree view of the user record. IDDM can span multiple HR platforms, directories, cloud platforms, IGA and PAM solutions, applications, risk engines, and flat files to create as rich and complete a user profile as possible. This Master User Record is then modeled into PE- and application-specific views tailored to the schema, structure, format, and protocol that each consumer of this identity data needs. The concept of “building it once, using it everywhere” not only greatly reduces integration costs and time, but also ensures that all security decisions across all PEs and applications are being made based on the same vetted data from sources of truth. The IDDM platform is capable of reflecting changes in near real-time from enabled systems, and scaling to hundreds of millions of users while maintaining necessary performance. IDDM supports the inclusion of additional objects from contractors, partners, vendors, coalition partners, and non-person entities (NPEs).

records.architecture_component: Endpoint Security - Unified Endpoint Management (UEM)/Mobile Device Management (MDM)
records.component_function:
Manages and secures enterprise desktop computers, laptops, and/or mobile devices in accordance with enterprise policy to protect applications and data; ensure device compliance; mitigate and remediate vulnerabilities and threats; monitor for suspicious activity to prevent and detect intrusions; prevent, detect, and disable malware, viruses, and other malicious or unauthorized traffic; repair infected files when possible; provide alerts and recommend remediation actions; and encrypt data.
Pushes enterprise applications and updates to devices, enables users to download enterprise applications that they are authorized to access, remotely deletes all applications and data from devices if needed, tracks user activity on devices, and detects and addresses security issues on the device.
records.relationship: Supports (example of) SM 2.3: Protect data at rest by encrypting the sensitive data used by critical software and critical software platforms consistent with NIST’s cryptographic standards.
records.relationship_explanation: The UEM/MDM may encrypt data stored on the device, but data stored on the device could also be encrypted via a different mechanism.

May include mechanisms that are designed to protect applications and data; ensure device compliance with policies regarding hardware, firmware, software, and configuration; monitor endpoints for vulnerabilities, suspicious activity, intrusion, infection, and malware; block unauthorized traffic; disable malware and repair infections; manage and administer software and updates; monitor behavior and critical data; and enable endpoints to be tracked, troubleshooted, and wiped, if necessary.
Supports (example of) SM 4.4: Employ network security protection to monitor the network traffic to and from  critical software platforms to protect the platforms and their software using networks.
The EDR/EPP can monitor the device for unauthorized network connections. Other network monitoring technologies can be used instead of EDR/EPP to do this.

records.architecture_component: Policy Decision Point (PDP), which consists of the Policy Engine (PE) and the Policy Administrator (PA)
records.component_function: The PE decides whether to grant, deny, or revoke access to a resource based on enterprise policy, information from supporting components, and a trust algorithm. The PA executes the PE’s policy decision by sending commands to a PEP that establishes and shuts down the communication path between subject and resource.
records.relationship: Supports (integral to) SM 1.4: Employ boundary protection techniques as appropriate to minimize direct access to critical software, critical software platforms, and associated data.
records.relationship_explanation: The PE makes remote access decisions based on policy. In a ZTA, the PE must be applied to help manage remote access. Note that in ZTA, the same policy applies to all access requests, regardless of whether they are remote or local. Although ZTA does not differentiate between local and remote access policy, compliance frameworks might. The PA supports the enforcement of remote access decisions by conveying the access decision information from the PE to the PEP, where the decision can be enforced. In a ZTA, the PA must be applied to help manage remote access.

records.architecture_component: Endpoint Security - Unified Endpoint Management (UEM)/Mobile Device Management (MDM)
records.product: Ivanti Neurons for Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) Platform
records.component_function: Manages and secures enterprise desktop computers, laptops, and/or mobile devices in accordance with enterprise policy to protect applications and data; ensure device compliance; mitigate and remediate vulnerabilities and threats; monitor for suspicious activity to prevent and detect intrusions; prevent, detect, and disable malware, viruses, and other malicious or unauthorized traffic; repair infected files when possible; provide alerts and recommend remediation actions; and encrypt data. Pushes enterprise applications and updates to devices, enables users to download enterprise applications that they are authorized to access, remotely deletes all applications and data from devices if needed, tracks user activity on devices, and detects and addresses security issues on the device.
records.relationship: Supports (example of) SM 2.3: Protect data at rest by encrypting the sensitive data used by critical software and critical software platforms consistent with NIST’s cryptographic standards.
records.relationship_explanation: The Ivanti UEM encrypts data stored on the device using native encryption features enforced by the UEM policies applied to devices based on device groups or user groups. Ivanti supports native encryption technologies such as BitLocker, FileVault, iOS-native encryption, and Android-native encryption.

records.component_function:
Manages and secures enterprise desktop computers, laptops, and/or mobile devices in accordance with enterprise policy to protect applications and data; ensure device compliance; mitigate and remediate vulnerabilities and threats; prevent, detect, and disable malware, viruses, and other malicious or unauthorized traffic; repair infected files when possible; provide alerts and recommend remediation actions; and encrypt data.

records.component_function: Aggregates and correlates all attributes relating to an identity or object that is being authorized by a ZTA. records.product: Radiant Logic RadiantOne Intelligent Identity Data Platform
records.component_function: Aggregates and correlates all attributes relating to an identity or object that is being authorized by a ZTA. It enables users of one domain to securely access data or systems of another domain seamlessly, and without the need for completely redundant user administration. Federated identity encompasses the traditional ICAM data, supports identities that may be part of a larger federated ICAM community, and may include non-enterprise employees.
records.relationship: Supports (example of) SM 2.2: Use fine-grained access control for data and resources used by critical software and critical software platforms to enforce the principle of least privilege to the extent possible.
records.relationship_explanation: RadiantOne IDDM and IDA work together to provide and enhance the aggregation of identity attributes from multiple disparate sources in order to create, manage, clean, audit, and maintain a rich and diverse set of user identity attributes needed to provide fine-grained access control across the enterprise. Fine-grained access control provides a model to authorize access to resources at the time of request by the user based on defined policies and the evaluation of the attributes possessed by the user at the time of request. By authorizing access only when requested and removing it when the user no longer needs it, the platform avoids the overprovisioning of static access common in role-based models.  This is a critical component of the least privileged model designed to reduce the attack surface of every user’s account.

records.architecture_component: Endpoint Security - Unified Endpoint Management (UEM)/Mobile Device Management (MDM)
records.component_function:
Manages and secures enterprise desktop computers, laptops, and/or mobile devices in accordance with enterprise policy to protect applications and data; ensure device compliance; mitigate and remediate vulnerabilities and threats; monitor for suspicious activity to prevent and detect intrusions; prevent, detect, and disable malware, viruses, and other malicious or unauthorized traffic; repair infected files when possible; provide alerts and recommend remediation actions; and encrypt data.

Pushes enterprise applications and updates to devices, enables users to download enterprise applications that they are authorized to access, remotely deletes all applications and data from devices if needed, tracks user activity on devices, and detects and addresses security issues on the device.
records.relationship: Is supported by (precedes) ID.AM-1: Physical devices and systems within the organization are inventoried
records.relationship_explanation: For a device to be enrolled into a UEM/MDM system, the device must be known to be part of the organization’s inventory.

May include mechanisms that are designed to protect applications and data; ensure device compliance with policies regarding hardware, firmware, software, and configuration; monitor endpoints for vulnerabilities, suspicious activity, intrusion, infection, and malware; block unauthorized traffic; disable malware and repair infections; manage and administer software and updates; monitor behavior and critical data; and enable endpoints to be tracked, troubleshooted, and wiped, if necessary.
Supports (integral to) PR.AC-3: Remote access is managed
The EDR/EPP may include a firewall that blocks unauthorized connections to and from the device.

Creates and manages enterprise user and device accounts, identity records, role information, and access attributes that form the basis of access decisions within an organization to ensure the correct subjects have the appropriate access to the correct resources at the appropriate time
Supports (integral to) PR.AC-1: Identities and credentials are issued, managed, verified, revoked, and audited for authorized devices, users, and processes

IBM Security Verify supports issuance, storage, management, and revocation of identities and their associated roles and credentials. It also supports the verification of credentials when performing user and device authentication.

records.component_function: Manages access to resources by performing user and device authentication (e.g., SSO and MFA) and using identity, role, and access attributes to determine which access requests are authorized.
records.relationship: Is supported by (precedes) PR.AC-6: Identities are proofed and bound to credentials and asserted in interactions
records.relationship_explanation: IBM Security Verify supports the ability to determine whether an access request is authorized. It authenticates the user or device that is requesting access by verifying the credentials that are bound to the user or device and asserted as part of the access request. The user and device identities must be asserted for this component to be able to authenticate them.

records.architecture_component: Endpoint Security - Unified Endpoint Management (UEM)/Mobile Device Management (MDM)
records.component_function:
Manages and secures enterprise desktop computers, laptops, and/or mobile devices in accordance with enterprise policy to protect applications and data; ensure device compliance; mitigate and remediate vulnerabilities and threats; monitor for suspicious activity to prevent and detect intrusions; prevent, detect, and disable malware, viruses, and other malicious or unauthorized traffic; repair infected files when possible; provide alerts and recommend remediation actions; and encrypt data.
Pushes enterprise applications and updates to devices, enables users to download enterprise applications that they are authorized to access, remotely deletes all applications and data from devices if needed, tracks user activity on devices, and detects and addresses security issues on the device.
records.relationship: Is supported by (precedes) ID.AM-1: Physical devices and systems within the organization are inventoried
records.relationship_explanation: IBM Security MaaS360 involves device enrollment into a UEM/MDM system. The device must be known to be part of the organization’s inventory before it can be enrolled.

records.product: Radiant Logic RadiantOne Intelligent Identity Data Platform
records.component_function: Aggregates and correlates all attributes relating to an identity or object that is being authorized by a ZTA. It enables users of one domain to securely access data or systems of another domain seamlessly, and without the need for completely redundant user administration. Federated identity encompasses the traditional ICAM data, supports identities that may be part of a larger federated ICAM community, and may include non-enterprise employees.
records.relationship: Is supported by (precedes) ID.AM-6: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for the entire workforce and third-party stakeholders (e.g., suppliers, customers, partners) are established
records.relationship_explanation: The core function of the RadiantOne Identity Data Manager (IDDM) is to abstract identity and credential data from multiple disparate sources of truth and build an aggregated 360-degree view of the user record. IDDM can span multiple HR platforms, directories, cloud platforms, IGA and PAM solutions, applications, risk engines and flat files to create a rich and complete a user profile as possible. This Master User Record is then modeled into PE- and application-specific views tailored to the schema, structure, format, and protocol that each consumer of this identity data needs. The concept of “building it once, using it everywhere” not only greatly reduces integration costs and time, but ensures that all security decisions across all PE and applications are being made based on the same vetted data from sources of truth. The IDDM platform is capable of reflecting changes in near real-time from enabled systems, and scaling to hundreds of millions of users while maintaining necessary performance. IDDM supports the inclusion of additional objects from contactors, partners, vendors, coalition partners, and non-person entities (NPEs).

records.architecture_component: Endpoint Security - Unified Endpoint Management (UEM)/Mobile Device Management (MDM)
records.component_function:
Manages and secures enterprise desktop computers, laptops, and/or mobile devices in accordance with enterprise policy to protect applications and data; ensure device compliance; mitigate and remediate vulnerabilities and threats; monitor for suspicious activity to prevent and detect intrusions; prevent, detect, and disable malware, viruses, and other malicious or unauthorized traffic; repair infected files when possible; provide alerts and recommend remediation actions; and encrypt data.
Pushes enterprise applications and updates to devices, enables users to download enterprise applications that they are authorized to access, remotely deletes all applications and data from devices if needed, tracks user activity on devices, and detects and addresses security issues on the device.
records.relationship: Supports (integral to) AC-1: Policy and Procedures
records.relationship_explanation: UEM/MDM devices enforce access control policies and procedures and associated access controls.

Supports (example of) SC-39: Process Isolation

One way to secure cloud workloads is to segment the cloud data center into small segments, define security controls for each segment, and run one workload on each segment to protect individual workloads and isolate them from each other so malware and breaches cannot migrate from workload to workload. The cloud workload protection component may implement micro-segmentation or use hypervisors to isolate workloads.

records.component_function: The Appgate Injector (Appgate for Kubernetes) creates a per-pod secure connection to the PEP, enabling authorized service-to-service and service-to-resource communication without the Pod or the resource visible on the Internet.
records.relationship: Supports (integral to) AC-17: Remote Access
records.relationship_explanation: The Appgate Injector ensures that Service/Pod network traffic destined for protected resources is securely transmitted over mTLS tunnels to an Appgate SDP Gateway where mTLS encryption is removed and data passes in the native format/protocol to the protected resource. Services/Pods can be in the cloud or on-premises. Protected resources can be in the cloud or on-premises and do not need to be collocated with Services/Pods they communicate with.

records.architecture_component: Endpoint Security - Unified Endpoint Management (UEM)/Mobile Device Management (MDM)
records.component_function:
Manages and secures enterprise desktop computers, laptops, and/or mobile devices in accordance with enterprise policy to protect applications and data; ensure device compliance; mitigate and remediate vulnerabilities and threats; monitor for suspicious activity to prevent and detect intrusions; prevent, detect, and disable malware, viruses, and other malicious or unauthorized traffic; repair infected files when possible; provide alerts and recommend remediation actions; and encrypt data.
Pushes enterprise applications and updates to devices, enables users to download enterprise applications that they are authorized to access, remotely deletes all applications and data from devices if needed, tracks user activity on devices, and detects and addresses security issues on the device.
records.relationship: Supports (integral to) AC-1: Policy and Procedures

records.architecture_component: Endpoint Security - Unified Endpoint Management (UEM)/Mobile Device Management (MDM)
records.product: Ivanti Neurons for Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) Platform
records.component_function: Manages and secures enterprise desktop computers, laptops, and/or mobile devices in accordance with enterprise policy to protect applications and data; ensure device compliance; mitigate and remediate vulnerabilities and threats; monitor for suspicious activity to prevent and detect intrusions; prevent, detect, and disable malware, viruses, and other malicious or unauthorized traffic; repair infected files when possible; provide alerts and recommend remediation actions; and encrypt data. Pushes enterprise applications and updates to devices, enables users to download enterprise applications that they are authorized to access, remotely deletes all applications and data from devices if needed, tracks user activity on devices, and detects and addresses security issues on the device.
records.relationship: Supports (integral to) AC-1: Policy and Procedures
records.relationship_explanation: The Ivanti UEM enforces access control policies and procedures and associated access controls for devices under management. Applications, VPN tunnels, and proxy configs can be pushed or revoked based on access required for a device or user under management based on AD group/role.

Pushes enterprise applications and updates to devices, enables users to download enterprise applications that they are authorized to access, remotely deletes all applications and data from devices if needed, tracks user activity on devices, and detects and addresses security issues on the device.
records.relationship: Supports (integral to) RA-5: Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning
records.relationship_explanation: The Ivanti UEM can monitor device software, firmware, and configurations for vulnerabilities and threats. With Ivanti Mobile Threat Defense activated, the Ivanti UEM can apply remediation actions to devices with device, network, application, and phishing vulnerabilities.

source_fragments.text: Endpoint Security - Unified Endpoint Management (UEM)/Mobile Device Management (MDM)
Ivanti Neurons for Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) Platform

Manages and secures enterprise desktop computers, laptops, and/or mobile devices in accordance with enterprise policy to protect applications and data; ensure device compliance; mitigate and remediate vulnerabilities and threats; monitor for suspicious activity to prevent and detect intrusions; prevent, detect, and disable malware, viruses, and other malicious or unauthorized traffic; repair infected files when possible; provide alerts and recommend remediation actions; and encrypt data. Pushes enterprise applications and updates to devices, enables users to download enterprise applications that they are authorized to access, remotely deletes all applications and data from devices if needed, tracks user activity on devices, and detects and addresses security issues on the device.
Supports (integral to) RA-5: Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning

The Ivanti UEM can monitor device software, firmware, and configurations for vulnerabilities and threats. With Ivanti Mobile Threat Defense activated, the Ivanti UEM can apply remediation actions to devices with device, network, application, and phishing vulnerabilities.

records.component_function: Used to provide remote users’ connectivity to on-premises or cloud resources.
records.relationship: Supports (integral to) AC-17: Remote Access
records.relationship_explanation: The Ivanti Neurons for Secure Access (nSA) services platform contains the Ivanti Neurons for Zero Trust Access (nZTA) Controller. Authentication, endpoint posture assessement, role-based access control (RBAC), and nZTA Gateways are all managed, maintained, and enforced by the nZTA Controller in conjunction with the Ivanti Secure Access Client (ISAC) and nZTA Gateways. Access to enterprise resources (applications and networks/subnets) has to be explicitly defined and granted to the respective designated groups of users; the ISAC client connects directly to the respective application locations via SSL/TLS transport to nZTA Gateways to protect data in transit. The nZTA Controller baselines user behavior for access applications based upon source location and time of day; if anything trends above or below the baseline, automatic action can be taken to reduce/change enterprise resource access.

records.component_function: Component that is deployed to be the front-end for an internal resource (whether located on-premises or in the cloud) and act as a proxy for it. Requests to access the resource are directed to the connector, which responds by initiating a secure connection to the PEP. A connector enables access to a resource to be controlled without requiring the resource to be visible on the network.
records.relationship: Supports (example of) SC-7: Boundary Protection
records.relationship_explanation: The Ivanti Neurons for Zero Trust Gateway is a key component which sits in front of enterprise resource locations and is managed and maintained by the nZTA Conroller. The nZTA Gateway is not known by the ISAC client until authentication and posture/compliance assessment is complete between the ISAC client and the nZTA Controller. The nZTA controller both dictates access to the ISAC client and informs the nZTA Gateway which explicit resources the user has access to. Resources not explicitly defined for the users are not accessible unless defined by a Secure Access Policy.

records.architecture_component: Policy Decision Point (PDP), which consists of the Policy Engine (PE) and the Policy Administrator (PA)
records.product: Lookout SSE (includes Secure Private Access, Secure Cloud Access, and Secure Internet Access)
records.component_function: The PE decides whether to grant, deny, or revoke access to a resource based on enterprise policy, information from supporting components, and a trust algorithm. The PA executes the PE’s policy decision by sending commands to a PEP that establishes and shuts down the communication path between subject and resource.
records.relationship: Supports (integral to) AC-3: Access Enforcement
records.relationship_explanation: The Lookout SSE service makes adaptive, policy-based decisions based on the context of the request. The context can include user identity, user risk, device posture, device risk, location, location anomalies, location risk, and more to determine if access should be granted to a resource. The policy engine follows zero trust principles to only grant access for the requested on-premises or private cloud-hosted resource. Lookout SSE enforces authorizations for access to information and system resources in accordance with applicable access control policies. Enforcement is performed at the hostname/IP(s), port(s), and protocol level of the defined protected resource(s) by leveraging numerous contexts of the request.

records.relationship: Supports (integral to) AC-2: Account Management
records.relationship_explanation: Lookout SSE redirects users to a SAML provider for user identification and verification to help determine what resources a user can access. Lookout SSE leverages the account information, as well as device, location, app information, and risk status to determine access. Lookout SSE controls the flow of information between the endpoint and requested resource. User activity works through the data plane while system-configuration activity happens across the control plane. The different planes are separate and do not interact. Lookout SSE enforces remote access decisions based on the requested resource, activity, and context of the request.

records.component_function: Restricts access to/actions on data based on permanent or transient attributes of the entity accessing the data, with the ability to revoke access as needed. Includes all data access policies and rules needed to secure access to enterprise information and resources.
records.relationship: Supports (example of) AC-16: Security and Privacy Attributes
records.relationship_explanation: Lookout SSE provides content rule management, allowing for the creation and use of organization- and industry-defined data detection attributes. Lookout SSE can leverage content rule management to look for multiple types of configuration data. In addition, Lookout SSE can apply, update, and leverage data classification markers to help detect confidential information. Data loss prevention rules identify sensitive data stored in SaaS and IaaS repositories. Detected data can be masked, redacted, encrypted, quarantined, or deleted, and collaborators or external shares can be removed. Lookout Data Loss Prevention can apply time-bound encryption to files in transit and at rest.

records.architecture_component: Endpoint Security - Unified Endpoint Management (UEM)/Mobile Device Management (MDM)
records.component_function:
Manages and secures enterprise desktop computers, laptops, and/or mobile devices in accordance with enterprise policy to protect applications and data; ensure device compliance; mitigate and remediate vulnerabilities and threats; prevent, detect, and disable malware, viruses, and other malicious or unauthorized traffic; repair infected files when possible; provide alerts and recommend remediation actions; and encrypt data.

Pushes enterprise applications and updates to devices, enables users to download enterprise applications that they are authorized to access, remotely deletes all applications and data from devices if needed, tracks user activity on devices, and detects and addresses security issues on the device.

Manages and secures enterprise desktop computers, laptops, and/or mobile devices in accordance with enterprise policy to protect applications and data; ensure device compliance; mitigate and remediate vulnerabilities and threats; prevent, detect, and disable malware, viruses, and other malicious or unauthorized traffic; repair infected files when possible; provide alerts and recommend remediation actions; and encrypt data.

Pushes enterprise applications and updates to devices, enables users to download enterprise applications that they are authorized to access, remotely deletes all applications and data from devices if needed, tracks user activity on devices, and detects and addresses security issues on the device.
Supports (example of) SC-8: Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity
Microsoft Intune provides cryptographic protection for transmitted information.

source_fragments.text: Endpoint Security - Endpoint Protection Platform (EPP)
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint

Detects and stops threats to endpoints through an integrated suite of endpoint protection technologies including antivirus, data encryption, intrusion prevention, EDR, and data loss prevention (DLP). May include mechanisms that are designed to protect applications and data; ensure device compliance with policies regarding hardware, firmware, software, and configuration; monitor endpoints for vulnerabilities, suspicious activity, intrusion, infection, and malware; block unauthorized traffic; disable malware and repair infections; manage and administer software and updates; monitor behavior and critical data; and enable endpoints to be tracked, troubleshooted, and wiped, if necessary.

The Global Secure Access (GSA) Client allows organizations control over network traffic at the end-user computing device, giving organizations the ability to route specific traffic to on-prem, cloud, and Internet resources.
